description: Agent Capacity: submit an agent’s concurrent runs with its concurrency cap: optionally the agent with its id and name; the cap with the most runs allowed at once, what holds it (a scheduler, a gateway, the platform, the agent itself or nothing) and the cap as written; each shared resource with its name and whether it takes one run at a time (exclusive) or many (shared); each run with its id, when it started and ended, the resources it holds, its outcome (completed, running, throttled or failed) and why a throttled or failed run stopped (contention, timeout, error or other); optionally the peak concurrency the system recorded; and the moment runs are read at. The signed report gives the cap with whether it is held outside the agent, the peak worked out from every run’s start and end with when it came, the runs at it, the recorded peak and the headroom left, every pair of runs that overlapped on an exclusive resource, and every run stopped for contention, and counts them, and names runs over capacity: more runs at once than the cap, runs overlapping on an exclusive resource and no cap at all; then a cap held only by the agent or by nothing, runs throttled or failed for contention and a recorded peak that differs from the runs, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No cap, no runs, open runs with no reading moment or resources with no stated mode leave concurrency unverified. This reads overlapping run times against the concurrency cap: one spending cap drawn by several agents is wever_shared-cap-check, one resource committed twice in collaborators’ recorded decisions is wever_coordination-conflict-check and the layer that enforces a rate ceiling is wever_limit-substrate-check. Verdict capacity_concurrency_over, capacity_concurrency_partial, capacity_concurrency_unverified or capacity_concurrency_within. POST /api/capacity-concurrency-check. Reads the load and capacity records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Capacity reads an agent’s own load and capacity records and checks the load against the capacity that exists: work in hand against the stated limit, a queue against its target wait, concurrent runs against the cap, an allowance’s burn against its period, a backlog across a window, spare capacity against the reserve, the scaling plan against the burn, and admission at capacity against written priority rules. Beside it, the Agent Limits checks such as wever_limit-substrate-check read whether a limit sits in code or in prose and how it is scoped, changed and seen, while a capacity check reads the load itself against the capacity; wever_commitment-deadline-check reads promised hours against due dates, while the workload check reads the work in hand against the stated limit over time; and the Agent Triage checks such as wever_triage-priority-check read how queue items are ranked, reviewed and closed, while the queue, backlog and throttle checks read waits, size and admission against capacity. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-capacity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-capacity/.

mode.description: Exclusive resources take one run at a time.

ended.description: A date or time, such as 2026-11-20 or 2026-11-20T14:00Z.

reason.description: Why a throttled or failed run stopped.
